A session was handed work when the agent wrote to it within the configured period (any message that reached it), or when the message names an open item the session moves now that the agent itself handed it (the item's hand-off record; having made the item or being its contact is not enough); a script, the person's own message, a peer front agent and fyi=true never qualify, and one session starts at most the configured number of such turns an hour in one agent (`[front] result_turn_cap_per_hour`; past that, or when the cap cannot be counted, the message is handled as below, held for the agent's next turn; two messages at the same moment can exceed it by a few). The result is also written onto the one to three open items it names, as a History line. The agent's reply to the session is itself a hand-over, so two sessions can wake each other: send fyi=true when a message needs no reply. A background agent's hand-back, a done, taken or no-action note, is tested first and is never an answer: written onto the item it names, else held. Any other unmarked message is delivered only as the answer to a question it wrote to you, while he is in that conversation (30 minutes); later it goes onto the item it names, else is held; so is a front peer's or a background agent's own. Any other goes to the project's background agent (none: held). A front agent marks a question with question=true; only a reply to it, within a day, is an answer; a `?` marks nothing. A done, taken or no-action note (a plain status report, nothing needed from the owner, FYI, no reply needed, …), marked or not, is held. A phrase is a note only as its own statement: opening a sentence or line, or ending a clause after , ; ( or a dash; not mid-sentence or asked. A marked one naming an open item of his is delivered anyway. A background agent's message to a front agent (marked, or a project message that opens For <front agent>) that names one to three board items is held back only when it clearly reads as a plain status report: the reply then begins 'Not delivered: written onto <item> as a History line ...' and the message sits on the item. It reads as a plain status report only when every sentence says done, live, merged, released, deployed, closed, opened, fixed, passes, green, recorded, unchanged, complete, finished, removed or retired (taken only as a sentence of its own, stopped only as 'is stopped'), and the text has no question mark (a URL's included), no prose in a code span, no plan (will, if, when, then), no person or front agent named to act, no opening yes or no and no word of trouble, lack, negation, waiting or asking (failed, blocked, need, must, review, ready, decide, please, not, yet, still, nothing, none, except, only, partly ...). A fixed no-action phrase skips only the status words. Everything else is delivered (the reply begins 'delivered'), and so is a message whose item waits on a decision (needs: decision) or names the front agent in its needs. A move to needs=decision reaches the owner on the board, not through a message. A merge-queue group number ("group g7", "[g7]") names no item. A message that asks nothing of its recipient is sent with fyi=true (news, a result, a status it need not act on): a background agent gets it with the first turn it takes, once (the reply begins 'held for <agent>'s next turn'), and it names the agent in no item's needs, so send it again without fyi if it does ask; to a project it is held the same way when the router passes it to an agent; to a front agent it is held for that agent's next turn (a listed one too), needs no [for the owner] and starts no turn ('not passed on' when its hook cannot fetch held lines); a message that carries [for the owner] or needs: decision is delivered, written onto its item or held whatever the flag says. A message to a retired session goes to its project for the router to rule, the reply beginning `'<name>' is retired (<why>), so this went to its project …`; it is refused only when no other agent of a project can take it. A page key spelled another way (case, - for /, projects/infra-x for infra/x) is read as the one page it matches, the reply saying so; none or two, refused with the nearest keys. A message to a project is answered `held for the router — the router rules notice <id> …`, ending `get(item_id="<id>") shows its ruling`: call get. The reply adds NOT PASSED ON when you move the item it names: write the item to hand a step on. A reply that begins `inbox` means the line waits in the server's inbox for the session's machine to fetch it (about a minute); if the session is running and the line is still there after 5 minutes, the fleet's keeper is told why, and so is the running pane that sent it (not a cloud or Cowork sender); a line held on purpose, by a relaunch hold or a pause, is not reported. The receiver sees a labelled [stackshot message] turn framed as a teammate's request, never as the owner's instruction or approval. A sender off the project's agents map gets a note naming its -main agent.

fyi.description: True when the message asks nothing of its receiver (news, a result, a status). A background agent or a front agent then gets it with its next turn instead of a turn of its own. Default false.

question.description: True when a front agent asks the session it writes to a question: only a reply to it is an answer. Not with fyi or in the owner's own name. Default false.

sender.description: Your own session name or id.

text.description: The message, at most 4000 characters. To a front agent its first line is [for the owner], then the item's plain id and what is needed; a plain result goes to projects/<slug> or onto the item.

to.description: Who gets it: a session name or id, or projects/<slug>, which the router rules.

route.description: If your session did not load the owner's standing rulebook at start (a cloud or Cowork session), call the rules tool first and follow it; it overrides defaults. A ruling on a notice delivered for a project. The router rules every notice of every project by itself (rules in code, then one thin call), so call this to overrule a wrong ruling. `notice` = the id at the end of the notice ("notice a1b2c3"); `ruling` = passed (handed to an agent: name it in `to`) | merged (folded into a digest) | archived (kept for later) | dropped (not worth anyone's attention); `reason` = one line the owner can skim; `sender` = your own session. Right call: route(notice="a1b2c3", ruling="passed", to="my-x", reason="belongs to the export work", sender="my-x"). Call it once per notice, after acting on it; call it again to overrule an earlier ruling. The project's routing page (behind its number in the board's anchors column) lists every notice with its ruling and reason, and the board flags notices left without a ruling for over an hour. A held item that waits on the notice's anchor is released by a passed or merged ruling, and by any ruling of a person's message (a bare laugh or ack on that anchor is one too).

rules.description: the owner's standing rules — the rulebook every Claude Code session on the owner's machines loads through CLAUDE.md (RULES.md, git-synced). A session that did not load it at start (cloud, Cowork) calls this once at the start of a task and follows it; a session that has it does not. profile="cowork" (default) = the Cowork view: CLI-only sections replaced by their Cowork equivalents, incident notes stripped; profile="full" = the whole file. The rulebook parts named in config (skill files that CLI sessions load through hooks) are appended after the rulebook, each under "## Part: <name>".

sessions.description: If your session did not load the owner's standing rulebook at start (a cloud or Cowork session), call the rules tool first and follow it; it overrides defaults. the owner's Claude sessions and machines, from the live fleet state on the server box — for a session that cannot read it itself (on another machine, in the cloud, in Cowork). Each session: its name, its link (for a pane, the URL the fleet tool's store gives it, where one is configured; for a cloud or Cowork session, its claude.ai link; link a session by it; empty = no link, name it plainly), its machine, and its role where a project page names it (front agent, slack agent or background agent of <project>; a slack agent is a front agent that answers the Slack app's messages; a front agent takes a turn only on [for the owner] on its first line). Each machine: online or offline, its Claude Code CLI version, and on the box that runs it the fleet operator (the session a recycle or CLI-update cue goes to — from a cloud or Cowork session, relay the cue with message(to=<that name>)), live or not running. Cloud and Cowork sessions are listed when they own an open board item. name: optional case-insensitive filter on session names.

update.description: If your session did not load the owner's standing rulebook at start (a cloud or Cowork session), call the rules tool first and follow it; it overrides defaults. Update an item; only the fields you pass change. A sender off the project's agents map gets a note naming its -main agent: ask it to list you. Right calls (sender = you): steps 1 "my-x: build it" and 2 "my-x: test it" open, step 1 done: update(item_id="board#N", sender="my-x", done=[1], next="my-x: test it\nmy-x: open the PR") (next lists every open step of yours that stays); reword an open step: reword={"2": "my-x: ship the export"}; drop a step: dropped=[2]; work: the status of your open step, one line per call: work={"text": "PR 83 up", "state": "in progress"}; park for a work window: until="<last day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD>", wait_kind="time", wait_basis="soak ends <that day>" (the basis names its date, YYYY-MM-DD; it goes with a date past 7 days; within them his recorded words stand in); a wait until a date on your own item: until="<tomorrow or later, within 7 days, YYYY-MM-DD>T04:00", wait_reason="the nightly run finishes at 03:00"; wait on another item: after=["board#N"], until="<day, within 7 days>"; description="- Goal: the export finishes in under a minute\n- Problem: the nightly run takes 9 minutes" (short `- ` bullets, never a paragraph; every line, `- ` included, at most 120 characters, at most 8 lines); close: the complete tool. status: open | completed (`needs` says whose move it is). A close (complete, or update with status=completed) carries outcome: done | dropped | superseded (superseded_by = its id), reason (one line, at most 120 characters (longer is refused)) and outcome_text (`- ` bullets, every line `- ` included at most 120 characters); it clears next, ask and needs (and any park, until date or recycle wait), leaves the description as it was (one passed with a close is stored as outcome_text) and keeps due as a record. Reopening (status=open on a completed item) takes a new next, and drops outcome, outcome_text, reason and superseded_by. A close ticks only the steps that are still open and are yours (you wrote them, or they open with your name), by the closer (done when the outcome is done, dropped otherwise; this settles a step of his too). A step that opens with another session's name stays open, so the close is refused, naming that step: ask that session to finish it, or mark it in the closing call with update (status=completed and done=[n] or dropped=[n]; complete takes no marks). It tells the mover of every other open item that names the closed item (board#N), one message per mover (the first 8, then a count); the items that wait on it through after are woken; the closer is not told. A close that leaves out outcome, reason and outcome_text is accepted when the item has no open step and at least one step done (steps marked in the same call count): the server closes it as done, writes "closed with every step done (set by the server)" as the reason and "- every step is done (set by the server)" as the outcome bullet for the parts left out ("done or dropped" when a step was dropped; also for outcome="done" sent with the reason or the bullet left out), keeps the parts given, and says so in the reply; with an open step (named by number), no step done or no step at all, with any argument besides outcome, reason, outcome_text (or description), superseded_by, said, done and dropped, marking a step of his, on an item that waits on the owner in any form (needs=decision or his name, an ask, options he has not answered, a your-call or your-step, mover=the owner, a step line of his still open), or with a done check not passed, nothing is written and the item stays open. The server takes an ask off the owner's move in one case only: its author's own plain sentence. A write by the ask's author whose whole new text, in every text parameter of the call (description, next, subject, goal and the others; a line sent again whole from before is not new), is exactly one sentence, "The ask is wrong.", "My question is moot." or "This ask is no longer needed." (also stale, void, obsolete, no longer valid; at most one "- " bullet before it, and only "now", "anymore" or a full stop after it) removes the ask, its options and his stored your-call, hands the item back to its author, says so in History and in the reply, and keeps his late answer as a comment. Any other new line or sentence in that write (a hedge, a label such as Note:, a quote, a question, another language) means no word, and a write with no sender counts for nothing. A dropped dependency removes nothing: a gate is a precondition, so a dropped gate often makes the ask more live. When an ask whose text names an item after/once/when/until/waiting for/depends on has that item closed as dropped after the ask was written, the ask's author is reminded on each of his writes to the item while that item stays dropped and the ask stands (withdraw the ask with clear_ask=true if it is moot, otherwise it stands). The server never writes an ask, closes an item or answers for the owner. A new or reworded open step that opens with a front agent is refused on an item another session moves: open it with the mover's name, or send `For <agent>,` to its project page (a step it already holds stays). With no builder there, its front agents may take the item by mover= or a step behind an open step (the item moves to it, told, when the step before is done). A date alone is a wait: the item waits until that date. Work: Written by the mover or a session named in needs. A plain write by a background agent that is not in needs adds it there, and `then` follows the first session in needs; a write that sets needs itself, parks the item or only files it does not: to leave an item again, pass needs without yourself. subject (a create's, or one an update sets): the work that closes the item, read at a glance as a task (an English imperative, "Keep hand-off times on closed items"; in Korean, ending in -hagi or a noun task); never a symptom ("X fails when Y"), a statement ("X is live"), a "should" or "must" sentence, a question ("Should X change?") or a bare topic ("X settings"); at most 80 characters, the scope prefix counted; a longer one is cut at a word (the reply says so): the rest goes in the description bullets. An update that leaves subject out or sets the stored one is never refused for its length. description: the item's background as `- ` bullets of live state, one fact each: at most 8 lines, and every line, `- ` included, at most 120 characters (a link counts by its text); a longer bullet is split for you at a sentence end or a space (the reply says so); prose, a bullet that cannot be split (one unbroken token) and more lines are refused. The first bullet opens `Goal:` (`goal:` or a bold label is put right) with the finished outcome that work reaches, in a sentence; a symptom, cause or trigger goes in a later bullet that opens `Problem:`. Then what the item is and where it lives (his words as a bullet such as `- the owner: …`; parallel bullets go under one parent bullet, indented two spaces); never steps or commands for the owner (those go in step, below: how to do it, such as where to click or what to attach, as `- ` lines under his step; a bullet like that in the description is moved there), no working notes, status or history; prune what is no longer live; details go on the project page. A create, or an update that replaces the description, whose first bullet is no goal is refused; an update that leaves description out is never judged. A refusal lists the faults it can check together. Item text renders as markdown (nested `- ` lists, **bold**, `code`, > quotes; no raw HTML, headings or tables). next: the item's checklist: one step per line, in order, opening with who takes it (`<session>:`, `the owner:` or the outside party's name; a role may follow the name, `my-x (builder):`; a space follows the colon); a line naming no one (`Status:`) is refused, and a `- ` line under a named step belongs to it. the owner's steps are made by the server from the ask and the step and ticked by his answer: never write or mark them. Mark your step done=[n] when it is done and dropped=[n] when it is no longer wanted; never reword an open step to add progress, and a parked item still has the open step its date leads to. Results, PRs, commit ids and test counts go on the project page, never in next. A session's writes are refused: (1) a line of next that opens with no `<actor>:` (right: `my-x: open the PR`, or an outside party, `Acme support: reply on the invoice`; `Status:` and `Note:` are no actor, `my-x:do` with no space after the colon is refused); (2) on an update, an open step reworded in next alone (its text with words added, the old step left unmarked): keep the step as it is, mark it done=[n] when the work is finished, or write a different action as a new line (a step marked dropped=[n] may be replaced by a longer one); progress goes on the project page, never in a step (to give an open step other words, pass reword={n: "<new text>"}); (3) a write that leaves an item that stays open with no open step in next: name who takes the next step, keep one open step (a parked item's is the one its date leads to), or close the item with complete, which is exempt; the owner's server-made step counts. A step with a commit id, a test count, a merged, live or deployed status or a "since 09:30" stamp is written all the same and the reply notes it. A line of next is refused unless it is <= 200 characters after its `<actor>: ` prefix, and <= 280 in all (a link counts by its text); only the text you write in a call is checked. Each line remembers the session whose write put it there, and a later update changes only its own sender's lines. A command the owner runs goes in a next line that starts `the owner:`, whole in backticks, never in the description or in the step (step=…: a one-line summary, see step below); his item page shows it in Your step as its own block with a copy button. A next line that starts `the owner:` and asks him to run something (an imperative run cue such as run, type, execute, enter, or a place phrase such as "In a terminal:"; a line where someone else runs it, "say go and I will run …", is not a cue) gets the command check on create and update, refused as `next line: …`, and only for the lines the call sets: the command goes in backticks or a fence. A line that only mentions a command, and lines for other sessions, are not checked. A `! ` line (a command typed into a pane) in a line that starts `the owner:`, bare, in backticks or after a colon or a run cue ("type ! cmd"), is refused whether or not the line asks him to run it: put the command in backticks; "done!" is not a `! ` line. A first line of next that starts `the owner:` (or `you:`, "the owner to …") on an item that is doing, blocked or verifying is refused when the call sets next, needs or the step: set step=<his step in one line>, or needs=decision with an ask (a create has no step). A next line that defers on another item in words (once, after, when, until or before, then a board#N; the words of [keywords.model_guards] defer_after_id also count) is refused unless after=["board#N"] names that item in the same item, since a wait written only in words wakes nobody when the item closes; give the wait its end too, until=YYYY-MM-DD, the day it comes back to someone if board#N is still open (supplies=<what that item's output gives this one>). Right: next="my-x: ship the export once board#N closes", after=["board#N"], until="<day, within 7 days>". Only the lines the call sets are checked; a line that only mentions an item ("see board#N") is not a deferral; on an item waiting on his call (needs=decision) write "see board#N", not after=; until=YYYY-MM-DD is the way to be reminded on a day. Links sit on the words (`blocked on [#7](url)`), never a naked URL or a bare id: a naked http(s) URL in next or ask is refused, in a description it becomes a link to itself; write `[words](url)` (a code span or fence is fine). needs: whose move it is now (the list is described below). due: YYYY-MM-DD UTC, set only from a real deadline (the owner's word, an outside date, or a date a dependency fixes), otherwise left empty: a made-up date reads to the owner as their own deadline (to expect something back by a date, use until). ask: the line a needs=decision item carries, written so the owner can decide from it alone and refreshed whenever the question moves, one line of at most 240 characters with all four parts in this order, joined by " · ": "Decide: <what to decide> · Recommend: <your recommendation> · Stakes: <what happens either way> · By: <a date in words such as Mon Jun 8th 2099, or no date>"; example: ask="Decide: whether to approve the sample schema · Recommend: Approve · Stakes: waiting a week delays the demo · By: Mon Jun 8th 2099", options=[{"label": "Approve", "line": "Approve the schema", "recommended": true}, {"label": "Decline", "line": "Wait a week", "recommended": false}]. An ask that only confirms the owner's own action is refused ("have you done X?", a bare "is it done?", or a Decide part that names the action of his own `the owner:` next lines, such as "Decide: install the apps and delete the test repo?"): use step="<his action>" instead (on a create, set it by update after); a real choice between alternatives, a judgement ("have you decided …", "does it work for you?") and an Approve/Decline go-ahead stay decisions. One decision per item: an ask that packs several decisions, or points at choices by a number or letter code the item does not spell out (“choices 2-3”, “2b”), is refused: split it into one item per decision and write each option out in words in the ask or the description, so that the owner can decide from the item page alone. The Decide part asks one question, and its answers are the options: a second question joined to it (", and say if …", "and tell me whether …", "and decide whether …", "and whether …", ", and which …", "and, if so, …" when the clause ends there, a second question after a question mark; "Use A? Or B?" is one question) is refused: ask the first now and put the other on its own item, or fold it into the options. A bundled action ("retire the queue and also allow its jobs to drain") or a conditional ("merge now and, if green, release tomorrow", "approve it and, if so, start Monday") is one decision and passes. An ask that approves or picks a design, plan, proposal, draft, spec or migration package (“approve the six-part design”) links it in the ask line itself, as [design](https://…) or a bare https URL, or the write is refused: a link only in the description, a path on a machine or a summary is not the page the owner opens from the question; a short link text keeps the line within its character limit. A subscription or payment plan ("the hosting plan renewal"), a software package ("the package update") and a compound ("the design system rollout", "the spec change") name no design and need none. A decision to change wording quotes the current and the proposed text, labeled before and after, in the description or the options' lines. A needs=decision item whose description or next links a mockup (a https://claude.ai/artifact/… page, or a /mockup/<n> page of the fleet tool's web UI (host set in the instance config)) puts [mockup](<that link>) in the ask's Decide part too, or the write is refused: the home row and the item page show it as Mockup ↗ beside the question. A mockup link goes in the ask only: an option label or line holding a markdown link or an http(s) URL is refused. The link in an ask is a short decision page made for it (an artifact, a document, or a mockup page of the web UI) with the decision, its choices and what is at stake on it, never a long project or notes page: where the instance lists such pages, an ask that links one is refused when the write sets it, and so is an option that links one (an option holds no link: the short link goes in the ask's Decide part). options: for a pick between alternatives, one per line, options=[{"label": "<a short name>", "line": "<one sentence, at most 160 characters>", "recommended": true}, {"label": …, "line": …, "recommended": false}, …] (2–6 entries, exactly one recommended); the ask's Recommend names the recommended one's label. The server refuses a needs=decision item whose ask or description names alternatives while it lists none: words such as "which of the two", "pick one", "x, y or z", "x vs y", "Option A", and labeled choices in the Decide part ("A or B", "A (…) or B (…)", "A: … or B: …"); put each alternative in as one option, or the page draws only Yes / No for it. A needs=decision item with no options whose Decide part opens with what, which, how, who, when, where or why is refused (create; an update that sets the ask or options or puts it on his call), since Yes / No cannot answer it: list its answers as options or reword it as a yes/no ("Decide: whether to …"). The same goes for a needs=decision item with no options whose Recommend part is not a yes or a no (it names a person, a topic, a date, whatever the Decide part's wording or language), since the page draws only Yes / No under it: put the choices as options, or make it a yes/no question with a Recommend of yes or no. The ask line never says "I", "you" or "me" (the reply notes one; write "Pat unpublishes", not "I unpublish"). A yes/no decision lists two options, "Approve" and "Decline" (the one you recommend marked recommended: true), so the owner gets one-click buttons. options="none" clears them (refused while the ask is an open question). Write the project page first, then the board: a page write up to five minutes before the change counts. A description that changes the Goal sentence's words, with no new subject, gets one reply line quoting the stored subject (a note, never a refusal): send subject= if the title's work no longer reaches it. Words are compared: case, the spacing and punctuation between the same words and bold, code or link marks are no change; a word split or joined ("Re-run" to "Rerun") and a changed symbol (% and ~ count) are. A new subject, a changed Goal sentence or a first Goal that leaves an open item titled as a question, a statement or a should sentence gets one such line too: send subject= as the task. next replaces only your own lines: every line of next remembers the session whose update wrote it (the sender, or the item's creator when the call names none; not the name the line starts with). next=<lines> takes the place of the lines you wrote before, where the first of them stood (at the end when you had none) and leaves every other session's lines where they are; a step of yours that it leaves out stays open unless marked (done, dropped, reword). next="none" removes only your own lines; clear_next=true wipes every line, whoever wrote it, and with next given the wipe comes first and your lines are then set. A line of yours that another session's open line already reads the same is not added a second time. A close clears next whoever wrote it. ask="none" clears it (so does clear_ask=true). A write that leaves an ask standing on an item you move or wrote ends with a one-line reminder to withdraw the ask if it is wrong or moot; a write that sets an ask shows the owner's comments and notes since the item's last ask, so one that already answers it is seen before you ask again. His note on a step that only says he did it ("ran it"; "run it" is a request and ticks nothing) ticks the step, and one in which he says he will do it later ("I'll do it tomorrow evening") parks the item until then; any other note (a question, a negation, a deadline, more than that) goes to the session to judge. The ask's mockup rule above also holds on an update that sets the ask, description, next, needs or options or puts the item on needs=decision. options=[] (or "none", or clear_options=true) clears the options, which need no recommended one then (refused while the ask is an open question; a non-empty list still takes 2 to 6 entries, exactly one recommended). When the owner answers by picking an option, the server clears the ask and the options itself and keeps his answer with the option's label and line. A client whose tool has no ask parameter refreshes the ask by writing the new line, in the ask's form, as the first line of next. When this work settles or changes a premise of another open item, update that one too, in the same turn. item_id: board#N; a bare number N or #N is read as board#N (the reply says so), in a close too; the same for after and superseded_by. until takes YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM for a time of day, UTC; a full ISO time with seconds or a UTC offset is converted to that minute in UTC, and the reply says so. At that moment the server tells the item's mover and the sessions in its needs once and drops the date. A doing item whose date is over an hour away and whose every open step waits for a later date ("after Mar 2", "until Mar 2"; a deadline such as "by Mar 2" or "due Mar 2" is no wait) is listed as waiting, and the audit asks why the step cannot run now. Parked = an open item waiting until its next move is due: until with wait_kind="time", with what it waits for; at its date the server releases it, tells the sessions in its needs (else its mover; refresh the ask then) and returns it to the lane its needs give it. Meanwhile it reads as parked (a waiting state), not as work moving on agent; needs and due stay as they are. A write to an item whose needs hold decision drops its park (its date stays). Park his call instead, from a decision item or a doing item: needs=["<session>"] (the session that picks it up at the date; a front agent will do), until=<YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM>, wait_kind="time" (or event, relay, item where the wait stands on more than the date), wait_basis="<what the date is, with its date YYYY-MM-DD>" and mover=the owner; the ask and options stay on the item, and at the date they come back to him: a decision item returns with its ask and options, a doing item with its ask if it had one. Without wait_kind an item with him as mover and a date is refused as having nothing for him to do. A park of 7 days or less needs his recorded words (said=[Acked-by …], or his answer on the item); a longer one needs a wait_basis. the owner parks on his word. A park always names what it waits for: the owner's words, the items that must close first (after), a notice from an anchor scoped to the item, a pane recycle (recycle=true), or the end of a window the work itself needs; a park with a date and none of these is refused. A park with no date is not refused: the server stores a backstop day 14 days out (with a wait_basis that names a date ahead, that date; with a wait_kind, that kind's date as above), marked as set by the server and said in the reply, and its mover replaces it with the real day; never while the item waits on the owner in any form (the wait text above), so a park of his call always gives its date. Work moving in real time stays on agent however long it takes (a build, tests, a review, a release or its queue, a run or subagent of yours): do not park it: its mover's park is refused while its subagent runs on it. A session parks its own item when the work itself needs a wait-and-see window (a soak, a log or data collection window, a trial week, a timer it started): until=<when the window ends>, wait_kind="time", wait_basis="<what the window collects> ends <YYYY-MM-DD>" (a window of 7 days or less on your own item is a bare until with wait_reason). A session does not park to defer work it could do now: an item not parked is one its mover can move now, so work it in your next free turn. A date that is no park, whose next says the work waits for that day ("collect logs until <that day>, then review") gets a note on the reply, never a refusal: the item stays on agent and the note gives the park form above. When your write sets or keeps a date with no park over an hour ahead, you are the item's mover and every open step opens with a time at the date's hour or day ("at 03:00", "on <that day>", "tomorrow at 9"), the server parks it itself (parked, wait_basis from your wait_reason; the reply says `(parked: …)`); to work a step now, write it as the action and pass clear_hold=true. A next line that says in words it waits for an open item, a pull request's merge or release, a machine coming back online or a link, while the item stores no wait for it, is set by the ten-minute pass when the line is the item's only open step and one thing is named (after, an event wait, an anchor wait, or a step proof): clear_after=true, clear_wait=true or step_proof="none" sends it back and the server leaves that line alone. Steps started by an outside event ("when the next release lands") get a note instead: park with until, wait_kind="time", wait_basis, wait_reason (needs=external for a named outside party's reply). Neither applies to an action to take now, another party's step in flight, or an item not on agent (parked, waiting on the owner's decision or an open after item, needs=external, outside, verifying, blocked). An item that waits on another item is not parked but names it: after=["board#N"]. Nor is one that waits on the owner: needs=decision with its ask, after=<the item that carries the ask>, or his call parked as above. An item that waits on a named person outside (needs=external) is not parked, unless the thread it waits on is anchored to it (anchors(project, add=[url], items=[its id])) and named in next: park that one with a backstop date (until, at most [waiting] cap_days out unless his words are on the item), since the notice may never come; the server releases the park when the project's router (or the project's builder, else its -main agent) passes or merges a notice from that anchor (never when it drops one; in a project nobody rules, when any notice from it arrives), and tells the sessions in its needs (else the project's builder, else its -main agent). clear_hold=true releases it now (its date goes with it); until="none" drops the date: an item that waits on nothing else is active again, and a park stays only when an after, an anchor or a recycle still holds it. mover hands the item over: set mover=<session> (then=<who takes it after the owner's answer or step>, kept only while he is the mover; on an item a session moves it is dropped with a note) and the new mover is told; a front agent gets no hand-off notice, so an update from another session that sets mover or then (or post_wake_mover, the old name of mover) to a front agent gets the project's builder instead (the reply and History say so; send it again to keep it as sent; the one exception is a hand-back: the front agent holds the item's first open named step as the item stands before this write (a step line this call adds does not count, and the call leaves that step open), the front agent is a live front agent of the item's project, and the sender is the project's builder or the item's mover when that is no front agent: it is kept as sent at once, and a mover is told it is handed back, as a turn; with no builder it is refused, except from a listed session to a front agent of the item's project; a sibling front agent is kept on the owner's words in said, see mover); take over another session's item only when asked; a session about to be retired first hands over or completes its open items. mover=the owner alone is refused on an item that is doing: it needs step=… or needs=decision with ask=… in the same write (the refusal says so). An update that leaves an open item in a state that is the owner's (his step, or needs holding decision) and names no mover sets mover=the owner itself and moves the stored session mover into then (set then=<you> to have the item come back to you), and the reply ends with a `(mover: <session> → …)` note; when a save ends his state the mover he held goes back to then; a write that names the mover or clears it (clear_mover), a rename, priority or project write, a re-bullet and a close are left alone. When an item's work moves to another project's session, hand the item over in the same turn: mover = that project's user-facing agent (or the background agent doing the work), project = its page. The creator is not moved with it. owner, the old name of mover, is accepted for a few more days with a note in the reply and then refused: say mover. sender = your own session (name or cse_… id) when you edit an item you are not the mover of (a session named in needs always passes sender=<itself>): the page update the edit owes is then yours, not the mover's (a create, a complete, or an update to description, next, needs, status, due, after, or the park and its date owes one). While the GitHub mirror is on, sender is required on every update, confirm and complete, the mover's own included. Pass clear_needs=true (or needs="none") to remove the needs badge, clear_check=true (or check="none") to remove the done check, clear_due=true (or due="none") to remove a date that no longer holds (a postponement with no new date). priority: p1 | p2 | p3, shown but not sorted. project re-files the item under another page (projects/<slug> or infra/<slug>; pass the page `(filed on X)` names, never the shown top-level key). A state change also confirms the item (it reads fresh again); the confirm tool says it is still true without changing it. recycle=true: the item's work waits for the panes to be relaunched (a connector re-login, a settings, hook or plugin change, a CLI update; not a change to a connector's tools, which claude.ai refreshes on its own within about a day); set it only once the change it waits for is installed (merged and deployed, or provisioned), never before: an early flag recycles the panes too soon, for nothing (a flag set before the provision recycled the box too early). Set it on the item the change serves: a recycle is never an item of its own (create refuses one), and for a change no item covers, leave it for the next recycle (no idle-recycle command is configured); the fleet tool runs a flagged recycle itself, the board shows one "Pane recycle pending for … (the fleet tool runs it)" status line while an open item not parked carries it, and when the fleet tool reports the recycle done the server clears it and tells you to re-read the item and resume. clear_recycle=true takes it off by hand. A question the owner asks on an item (in his answer, a note on his step or a comment on it) is answered by the mover on the item itself, not only in its own pane: rewrite the description, and the options where it is a pick, the description saying it answers his question. A result he asks for there belongs on the item too. His question is never posted with said and never taken as his call; only his conclusions are. needs: whose move it is now, a list: "decision" (the owner's: decide, judge, review, give the go-ahead), "external" (someone outside, named in next) and session names (a background agent of any project, or the item's one mover; a user-facing agent that is not the mover is refused: its part becomes its own item, linked with after=), e.g. needs=["decision", "my-engineer"] or one comma-separated string. An item has one mover: a session named that is not a background agent of the item's project counts as a mover, and two of them, or decision beside one, are refused (name the one who moves it now, and who takes it after his answer in then=); a background agent of this project never counts as a second mover; empty means the item's mover (mover=, else the project's builder, else its -main agent) moves it. The lane follows the first of decision, external, a session (your call · on others · on agent). A session named is told when added, is asked about the item at each turn end and hears its date, recycle and after notices; it passes sender=<its name> on its writes, so they reach the mover as another session's. needs= replaces the whole list (name again what should stay); needs="none" or clear_needs=true empties it. decision vs your-step: needs=decision is the owner's call, a choice between options; a thing that is the owner's own to do is step=<his action> (update; a create has no step), and the board ticks it when he says it is done, so an ask that only asks whether he has done it is refused. agent=<session> is the older form: it makes that session the one named in needs (the decision and external entries stay); agent="none" takes the sessions out. observers: sessions that hear only a close or a reopen; observers="none" clears. tell_him: front agents he asked to tell him of it, a turn even while he is away; the write needs his words in said; "none" clears. after: items of any project that must close first (after=["board#N"]); while one is open the item counts as waiting without a park, and when the last one closes it wakes and the sessions in its needs (else its mover) are told; a dropped one releases it too, a superseded one is followed to its replacement; a loop is refused; after="none" clears. after is for a real dependency (this item needs that one's output), never for the order a builder takes its items in. A park (until with wait_kind="time") names what it waits for (a date, after items, an anchor notice, a recycle, or a wait_basis window); one that names none and gives no date is not refused: the server stores a backstop day 14 days out, marked as set by the server, and says so (replace it with the real day), unless the item waits on the owner in any form (needs=decision or his name, an ask, options he has not answered, a your-call or your-step, mover=the owner, a step line of his still open): then it is refused. An item waiting on the owner carries needs=decision with its ask, or after=<the item that carries the ask>; to park his call, see update (until with wait_kind="time", mover=the owner). needs names only who can move now. An item that waits on the owner and on a session at once: where his answer could change with the session's work, or its work with his answer, the session goes first and adds decision when it is done (or the decision is its own item, linked with after=); decision sits beside this project's background agents only when the two are independent (beside any other session it is refused), and when unsure, in sequence. When decision leaves needs (he has decided), the sessions still named are told at once; a session whose work changes the question rewrites the ask. The server hands no item to a front agent on its own motion: one back with its front mover alone tells the project's builder (the mover, if the project has no builder). check: what closes this item once the work handed to another session is done, a check the server runs itself every minute and, when it passes, closes the item with outcome done and a reason naming the check: pr_merged <owner>/<repo>#<n> (the pull request is merged), item_closed <id> (that board item is completed), lane <session> <lane> (the fleet tool's lane record puts that pane on that lane; only where one is configured), unit_active <unit>.service (the systemd user unit is active on the server box); nothing else, never a command. A check the server cannot read (GitHub down, a unit not found) never closes. A release of a pull request of the board's own repository needs no check: once main's full run passed on its merge and that merge is in the last-good commit and the live checkout, the server ticks a step that says it releases that PR (`release PR #<n>`, `release #<n>`, or `release` before the PR's URL; the step events, below, say what counts), only on an item anchored to that PR or naming its URL. An item whose only open steps are that release is completed, outcome done; on an item with any other open step the release step is ticked done and the mover told once. A step that only mentions the PR (investigate, review, verify) is never ticked and never closes the item. A parked item, or one whose needs name his decision or a session other than its mover, is left alone; a check that passes while the item waits on his decision does not close it until the decision is cleared. An update whose next hands the work to another session (a line of next in the form `<session>: <action>`, a list marker before the name at most: any session but the item's mover and you, not one already in needs; a name elsewhere, in a slug, a link or a sentence, hands nothing over) is refused unless the item carries a check or an until date, the hand-off's backstop: with a hand-off the date is no wait (unless the item is parked or carries wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait), the item stays active in the new mover's lane; a write that leaves an existing hand-off as it was is not asked again. Right: update(item_id="board#N", sender="my-x", next="other-x: build the export", check="pr_merged acme/widgets#12"). A front agent is the exception: its hand-off needs neither (a check stays allowed to anyone), because a front agent does not watch handed-off work itself: the result lands through stackshot when the mover closes the item or hands it back to you, so a front agent's own until date (no park) on an alive item another session moves is refused (a done check, a park with its until date stay allowed). To watch anyway, pass watch_reason=<why no push reaches you> (at least 15 characters) on update, in the same call; it is recorded on the item. check="none" clears it; a check alone owes no page. A check does not set the item's due time. check="" changes nothing, and a new check passed replaces the old one. Parameter contact (a filing field: it moves no state clock, changes no mover and sends no notice; get shows it as `contact:`): the front agent that the owner talks to about the item; the parameter says how it is set and when it falls to the project's -main agent. The item model (design: docs/design): an item is dead (closed), alive (someone in the perimeter is working: one mover) or waiting (nothing happens until something outside arrives). mover is how an item says whose move it is (the sender of a create is recorded as its creator). Optional fields, stored as given (each parameter says how it is set): goal=<the end-state in one sentence, what the owner would ask "is it done?" about>; mover=<who moves the item: on an alive item now, on a waiting item whoever takes it when the wait ends; the owner, a session name or the project's background agent; a front agent (a session the owner talks to) only by itself: a create or update from another session that sets mover to one gets the project's builder instead (see the mover parameter)>; then=<who takes it after the owner's answer or step; it stands only while he moves the item, and on an item a session moves or waits on it is dropped with a note in the reply: to hand an item on, set mover=<session>; then=<front agent> from another session gets the builder the same way>; wait_kind=time | anchor | item | relay | event; wait_anchor=<url of the anchor an anchor wait watches>, which must be on the project's anchors list first (add it with the anchors tool, scoped to this item), else the write is refused; wait_event=<what you expect there (an anchor wait), or the party or event the owner relays (a relay wait), or the fleet event an event wait watches: pr_released <owner/repo#n> | pr_merged <owner/repo#n> | recycle [<machine>] | fleet_op <verb | any | many> [<machine>] | job_run <name> | box_online <machine>>; until=YYYY-MM-DD (a relay wait's end day; an event, item or anchor wait's backstop day); post_wake_mover, the old name of mover, is still read as mover for a while (the reply says so; on an item that waits on nothing it is dropped, and a different mover beside it is refused). An event wait is how an item whose mover waits in the background for something the fleet does says so: update(wait_kind="event", wait_event="pr_released <n>" (this repository's pull request number), until=<the day it comes back anyway; left out, the server takes tomorrow or the day the item's words give, and says so; it is not the 14-day backstop>, mover=<who takes it then>). Live for now: pr_released, pr_merged, box_online, recycle, and every fleet_op form (any verb, any, many); a job_run wait turns only on its backstop day. box_online <machine> waits for a machine to be online (its puller checking in, within the minutes the server counts as online): the server reads it itself and the item turns within a minute or two of the machine's return, so an item waiting on a date for an offline machine says wait_event="box_online <machine>" with that date as until instead; the machine must be one the fleet knows (an unknown name is refused with the known ones). The backstop must be after now, and a day (until=YYYY-MM-DD) falls due at 00:00 of that day in the instance timezone, so today's date is already past: give tomorrow at the earliest (a relay or event wait takes the day alone: a time of day is dropped). A wait for something that has already happened (a PR already merged or live, a machine already online) is refused; a recycle wait never asks for a recycle (it waits for the next one). A step of his, or needs holding decision, makes him the mover: a write that names a session as mover beside it is refused (leave mover out, or mover=the owner, and put the session in then). The mirror is refused too: a write that leaves an open item with mover=the owner but in none of his states, so it has no step and no ask, is refused: pass step=<one line>, or needs=["decision"] with ask=…, or give the item to a session (mover=<session>) and write his part in a next line that starts `the owner:`. A waiting item, a close, a rename, a priority or project write and a re-bullet are not judged by it. A wait that replaces his state drops the mover, and the session in then picks the item up when the wait ends (it is stored as the mover). "none" clears a field; clear_goal, clear_mover and clear_then clear theirs, clear_wait the wait's fields (wait_kind, wait_anchor, wait_event, until). A close drops the mover and the wait and keeps the goal. The wait ends by itself when its kind's event comes: a time at its until date; an item when the last `after` item closes; an anchor when the anchor watcher's notice for wait_anchor reaches the server, and any new notice at the anchor that reaches the server and passes the project's keeper wakes the item; an event when the server is told of it; a relay on its until day, when it comes to the owner as a question (arrived / ask again in a week, two weeks or a month / not yet, ask again on a date / drop); a date beside it is its backstop. The item then turns alive with its mover. A moved until resets the backstop. Several waits at once are a list: waits (2 to 8 lines), wait_mode all | any, until as its backstop day; the item is back when every line has arrived (all) or the first has (any), at its until at the latest. Example: update(waits=[{"kind": "item", "after": "board#N"}, {"kind": "event", "event": "pr_merged <n>"}], wait_mode="any", until="<day, within 7 days>"). Send the lines that remain to edit it: one left is a single wait, waits=[] ends it. next is a checklist: the item keeps every step in the order written, open, done or dropped, and next holds the open steps. A step of yours leaves next only by being marked in the same update: done=[…] when the work was finished, dropped=[…] when it is no longer wanted, each entry a step's 1-based position (marked steps count; get lists them under `checklist:`) or the exact text of its first line (the call example is in the description above). An update that replaces or removes (next="none") your lines of next and leaves one out unmarked keeps that step open as written and the reply names it (end it with done=[n] or dropped=[n]); another session's lines are never touched by your next. Parameter reword (map, position or first-line text → new text) gives an open step of yours new words and keeps its number, place and open state (leave next out and the line is changed for you); a line reworded in next alone is a new step, and the old one stays open. A reword is the same action in other words, never the old text with progress added. A reword of a step of his (a line opening with `the owner:`) is done as drop plus add, and the reply says so: the old step is dropped and shows as dropped, and the new words are a new step at the end (a long text is split into one line per action, as for step=); a reword of the line the server made from step= is taken as the new step text, and one of the line made from an ask is refused with the field to change (ask=). Refused: a step of another session, one already done or dropped, one also in done or dropped, a text of several steps or one another open step reads; a different action is a new line of next. done and dropped mark any open step, whoever wrote it, except a step of his (a line opening with his name) while the item asks him: that one is ticked when he answers, and done on it is refused (dropped on it is undone while the item still asks him). The server makes his step itself: when an item asks him for a decision (needs=decision with an ask) or a step (your-step), it adds the open step `<his name>: <what to decide>` at the end (a line you wrote that says the same is adopted), shows his answer on it, and drops it when you withdraw the ask or the step; a step he already answered stays done. clear_next=true is a deliberate wipe: every line it removes becomes a dropped step, by you. A marked step stays on the page with who marked it and when; History says `step done: …` or `step dropped: …`. done or dropped alone, with no next, takes the step out of next; when two open steps read the same, the position names the one marked. A step written again after it was marked is a new step. the owner's word that his step is done checks every open step of his (each next line that starts `the owner:`); a note he sends ticks the step the server made and leaves your lines open for the session that takes the item to mark done. A step can name the event that finishes it, and the server then ticks it done when the event happens: a pull request merged (pr_merged), or released, i.e. merged and live (pr_released: this repository's with main's tests passed, or a configured repository's). A step that is only `release PR #<n>`, `release #<n>` or `release <URL>` (or the same with `merge`), with at most a short parenthetical (`(in its turn)`) and a closing full stop, is ticked when that pull request is released, on an item anchored to the PR or naming its URL. Anything else after the phrase (`and verify the pages`, `, restart x`, ` then …`) is a follow-up: the step stays open and its mover is told once; a condition (`once #<n> is released, …`, `when PR #<n> is merged, …`, `release it after #<n>`) is never ticked either, and its mover is told once it is met. A negated phrase (`do not release PR #<n>`), a step that only mentions the PR (review, verify, investigate), another repository's #<n> without its URL, and a step of his never match. step_proof=[{"step": <position or the step's exact first line>, "proof": "pr_merged <owner>/<repo>#<n>" | "pr_released <owner>/<repo>#<n>"}] states the proof outright, whatever the step's words say (a bare #<n> is this repository's, a URL works too; "proof": "none" clears one step's proof, step_proof="none" every one; the step must be open). When the event arrives the server marks the step done and tells its mover the next open step once; with no open step left the item closes, outcome done. A pull request closed without a merge ticks nothing. A done step whose next open step names another session makes that session the mover and tells it. A step that delivers a PR (`release`, `merge`) and is followed by another session's step must be only that phrase or carry step_proof, or the write is refused. draft: the text exactly as it is to be posted, sent or pasted somewhere else by the person whose step it is (a channel message, an email, a reply), as many lines as it has, stored and shown as written (no bullets, no line limit; at most 20000 characters). His item page draws it under the step as a block with a Copy button; a close drops it, and so does his Done or Send note on the step. A text a session can send itself (a Slack message, an email in his name, new or a reply) is not his step: it goes to him as a decision (needs=decision, an ask, the options Send / Change it / Don't send, the text in draft), and the session sends it when he picks Send; a step with a draft is for what only he can post or paste himself (an app or account a session cannot reach). An item whose step is such a post, send or paste carries the text: a write that sets the step or mover of an item so that it is his step, or that sets or clears its draft, with a step that names a text to post, send or paste (post, send, paste, reply, draft, message, email, share, forward, submit, and the instance's own words of [keywords.draft]; a heuristic, not a complete list), is refused unless the item has a draft or its step or description links the document that holds the text (an https:// link to a doc, Drive file, Notion page or Slack thread; a GitHub issue, pull request or commit link, or a link to the board, does not count). draft="none" (or update clear_draft=true) removes it; a create can store one before the step exists. step (update only; create sets no step): a ONE-LINE summary of what the person whose step it is does, for an item that is his step, at most 300 characters. How to do it (where to click, what to enter, what to attach, with its link) goes as `- ` lines under that line (a line indented under one belongs to it): the server keeps them beside the step, shows them under it on his home row and in Your step and in get under `step:`, never in next, and puts them back at the end of the description when the step ends. A how-to bullet of the description (a click path with two or more arrows, or attach or upload with a link) is moved under his step by your write (the reply says so: never a refusal), so the description keeps the background; a bullet with a command stays. A step sent again, reworded or split keeps the lines under it; step= with its own `- ` lines, or a description with new how-to bullets, replaces them, and the reply quotes what it replaced. It points at his Next lines and never holds a command: every shell command he runs goes in a next line that starts `the owner:`, whole in backticks (or a ``` block), never a `! ` line, the pane form, which is refused in a step and in a next line that starts `the owner:`, whatever else the line says. A step that carries a command (a backticked span with a space in it that reads as a shell command, a `! ` line, a ``` block) is refused, and the refusal says to put the command in a next line that starts `the owner:` (a step stored with a command before keeps the older checks on a write that leaves it alone). A button or menu label is not a command: put it in bold or quotes, not backticks ("Make a copy", **Sort by date**). A next line that starts with his name (`the owner:`) and asks him to run something gets the command check, on create and update, whatever the item's state, for the lines the call sets (the cue and the `! ` rule are under next above): a command outside backticks is refused as `next line: …`; a line that only mentions a command is not checked. A bare command with a flag, path or quoted argument, written outside backticks or a fence after a run cue or a place phrase ("In a terminal: ls -la"), is a command too: the step carries none, and a next line gets it in backticks so the board shows a copy box. A write that leaves an item for him to move (him as mover, in his step, or with his decision in needs) is refused when its description adds a numbered line (`1.`, `2)`) or a `! ` line outside a fenced block: the description is the background, never steps. A write that leaves an item in your-step for him is refused, in one line naming the field, when the description holds a shell command (move it to a next line that starts `the owner:`; a description write is judged only on the commands it adds or changes, and a fence there counts only when tagged sh, bash, shell, powershell, pwsh or console, and each command line of a tagged fence is judged; an untagged fence holds pasted output), or when the step points elsewhere ("see the description", "see below", or a phrase of [keywords.step_commands] pointer_patterns); a step that names his Next line passes. Only writes that set the state, step, mover, description or draft are judged, and [model] guards = false skips these checks. A wrong `stall:` step is undone with update (mover, next, clear_needs); the whole path, and why a pause needs the owner's own answer, is in get. A wait on your own item names its blocker: when the item's mover (you) sets an until date, or writes a line of its own next whose step is dated later than today (a date, "next week", "until Monday", "retry tomorrow", "after the weekend", "at the next nightly run"; a date after by, due, before, target or ETA is a deadline, no wait; a day named about the past is none), pass wait_reason=<what the step waits on that is not available now, at least 15 characters> in the same call, or the write is refused. With a reason, one model call judges whether the step could be done now: if it could, the write is refused with the model's reason, so do the step now or name the real blocker (a reply, a build or test still running, a window the work itself needs, a resource that is down; a preference for a scheduled run is none). The check passes the write when the model is unavailable or slow. It does not apply to a wait on another item (after), on a decision or an outside party (needs decision or external), a park (wait_kind="time" with wait_basis), a stored wait (wait_kind), a hand-off to another session, or a step you leave as it was. Right: update(item_id="board#N", sender="my-x", until="<tomorrow or later, within 7 days, YYYY-MM-DD>T04:00", wait_reason="the nightly run finishes at 03:00"). A step of next that names a machine of the fleet which is offline now (its fleet name or hostname as a whole word, an open step only) gets one `(note: …)` line in the reply when the item has no machine anchor for it and no box_online wait on it, naming the fix: anchors(project=<its project>, add=["machine:<name>"], items=[<its id>]) tells the item's mover each time that machine checks in again, without parking the item. A note, never a refusal. A reply may carry one `(anchor offer: …)` line: when the write set a relay wait on an item with no anchor scoped to it, or put a Slack, Gmail, Drive or Notion link in its description that no anchor watches for the item, the line carries the ready anchors call (the project and the item id filled in; a placeholder in angle brackets only for what the server cannot know, the person's thread). A note, never a refusal, and at most one a reply: make the call when news on that thread should reach the item, or leave it. A wait is one stored date, until, with wait_kind beside it when it stands on more than the date. An item with an until is waiting; the server clears both when the wait ends. wake and ask_by, and hold beside a date, are retired parameters: a call that passes one is refused, and the date goes in until. A wait_kind with no date is never refused: the server takes a date from the item's words, else a suggested one, else tomorrow, and says which; a park with a wait_kind and no date takes the same date, marked as set by the server. A wait this write would leave with no end day (an after link, a wait stored earlier, needs=external, a park, or a wait on a time with no date) is not refused either: the server stores its default backstop day, 14 days from today, marks it as set by the server and says so in the reply; a park sent with no date and a wait_basis that names a date ahead ends on that date instead (a basis that names none is refused as before). Its mover replaces that day with the real one (until). None of this while the item waits on the owner in any form, as it stands or as the write leaves it (needs=decision or his name, an ask, options he has not answered, a your-call or your-step, mover=the owner, a step line of his still open), nor when the item already holds an end in any field (an old ask_by included, past or ahead), nor beside a date of your own or "none" for one, nor in a write that clears or drops a wait or its end: the wait is judged as before, so one with no end is refused, and an end the item holds is never replaced. A list of waits still needs its until. The dates you give yourself keep the cap rules. Every open item has a mover (the one party whose move it is now: a session, the owner, an outside party, or the item it waits `after`). An open item waits on its real dates only (until, due): no expected time is derived for any item, and a parked item waits until its date or its blocker closes, with no stale mark. A date a session sets runs at most 7 days from the item's last move: a date further out, an anchored thread's included, is refused without the owner's words (said=[Acked-by …] checked against a transcript, a message from those days; or his answer on the item, given since its last move: ask him to answer there) or a wait_basis. A due date is a deadline and is not refused. Which wait to write: own work waiting on a date within 7 days: until="<tomorrow or later, within 7 days, YYYY-MM-DD>T04:00" with wait_reason="the nightly run finishes at 03:00"; a park for a window the work itself needs, or a date past the cap: until="<last day of the window, YYYY-MM-DD>", wait_kind="time", wait_basis="error-log soak ends <that day, YYYY-MM-DD>" (parameter wait_basis has the form; it goes with a date past the cap and with a stored verifying item's date, and lifts the cap for that date alone; clear_wait_basis=true drops it; a park of 7 days or less carries his recorded words instead, said=[Acked-by …] or his answer on the item, and a basis sent with such a date is dropped, the reply saying so). A bare date within the cap is a wait on its own and needs no basis; a date does not leave the item active as a reminder (outside a hand-off's backstop): set no date to keep an item moving. A wait that can no longer end (a check whose pull request was closed unmerged) fails at once and tells the item's mover. clear_wait=true is how an update drops a stored wait (wait_kind and its fields); wait_anchor or wait_event of none and clear_wait_basis do not. An update that newly adds needs=decision to an item that stores a wait is refused unless it also passes clear_wait=true: the wait would otherwise win and get would list a model conflict. clear_after=true clears the after list, as after=[] or after="none" do; some clients drop an empty list, so the flag always arrives. A write that clears a wait while an open next line still defers on what it cleared in words goes through, and its reply carries one line per stale next line (`(note: next line N still waits on board#X, whose wait was just cleared: reword it)`): reword or drop those lines in the same turn. An item stores alive or waiting directly; there is no state to set, and these are not parameters of this tool or of create: a call that passes state, clear_state, party, chase, end, proof or chase_note is refused with what to pass instead. Whose move it is goes in mover; the owner's call is needs=["decision"] with an ask; his own step is step=<one line, no command, of the single thing only the owner does, then how to do it as `- ` lines under it; what he runs goes in a next line that starts `the owner:`> (the board ticks it when he says it is done; never ask him "have you done it?" as a decision); a wait on another item is after=["board#N"] (supplies=<one line: what that item's output gives this one> says what it takes from it); a park is until=<date> with wait_kind="time" and either his recorded words for it (cap_ok) or a wait_basis (the end of a window the work needs, or a date past the cap); a wait on someone outside is wait_kind="relay" with wait_event=<who>, until=<the day to chase>, mover=<who takes it then> and needs=["external"]. Work in hand needs next and its mover and carries no expected time (the item shows how long it has run); expected_by and expected_reason, which older calls pass, are accepted and not kept (the reply says so). Work in hand is not a wait: a wait (a date, a timer, someone else's step or release) is parked the turn it starts, with update(until="YYYY-MM-DD" or "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", wait_kind="time", wait_basis="<what the date is, with its date YYYY-MM-DD>"), update(after=["board#N"]) for another item, or the relay wait above for someone outside (a write that leaves wait wording in next, such as overnight or once the vendor replies, gets a note saying to park it). No clock renewal without progress: a write that moves an until to a later time while the item's reason (description, wait_basis text) and its open steps are as they were is refused (a wait_reason does not count: it is not stored); in the same write mark a step done or dropped, write the next step or state a new reason (or send the owner's own words in said), or change what the wait stands on to a shape the item never held (wait_kind, wait_event, wait_anchor, after: a flip back to an earlier one does not count; such a shape change alone lets a clock push through twice and the third is refused, until a step, the reason, his new words or a hand-off resets the count); or, if the item now waits, park it (until, wait_kind="time", wait_basis) or use the event-wait form (wait_kind="event", wait_event, until, mover). Setting a first clock, pulling one in, clearing it and handing the item on are not renewals. On a parked item give a new wait_basis; an item on his decision cannot be parked. Take a date from the wait's real schedule (a timer, watch tick, catch-up run) or check it live, never a guessed round time. step=<one line> sets the item in his step and makes him the mover (then, or the agent that had it, takes it after his Done); step is a short summary, and a long one is put right for you: a step over 110 characters with several actions (sentences, semicolons, `1) … 2) …`) is split into a summary of at most 90 characters and one line of next per action that opens with `the owner:`, which the board draws as his list (a lead-in that ends with a colon before `1) … 2) …` is one line with its items as indented `- ` lines under it; the reply says so, no word is lost; send the summary and the lines yourself to choose the words); a long `the owner:` line of next with several actions is split the same way (never over 2000 characters or 20 actions, or with a word or code span longer than a line: a step over its limit is refused, saying why); a new step or step="none" drops the old split's open lines; step="none" withdraws it; supplies=<one line: what the item it waits after gives this one>, with after=["board#N"], sets the item blocked on that item. Each is refused without what it needs, with what to add; a close drops both. Checks: a next that opens with the owner: or you: under an agent's state is noted; the third bare re-park in a row is refused; a next may be marked stale; needs=decision again within 60 min of his answer is refused unless the ask changed. A reply names his answer given since your last write, unless told of it.

after.description: Items this one waits on: after=["board#N"], with until=<YYYY-MM-DD> as the day it comes back if they are still open (left out, with no wait_kind in the call, the server stores its default backstop day, 14 days from today, marks it as set by the server and says so; with a wait_kind it takes the next day or the day the item's words give; never while the item waits on the owner). The wait ends when they close.

ask.description: The one line a needs=decision item carries, all four parts in this order, joined by " · ", no line break, at most 240 characters in all: ask="Decide: whether to approve the sample schema · Recommend: Approve · Stakes: waiting a week delays the demo · By: Mon Jun 8th 2099" (By is a date in words, or no date). A real choice, not "have you done X?"; one question per ask, whose answers are the options (no ";" between decisions, no second question joined by "and say if", "and tell me whether", "and decide whether" or "and, if so, …" when the clause ends there; a bundled action such as "retire the queue and also allow its jobs to drain" or a conditional such as "merge now and, if green, release" or "approve it and, if so, start Monday" is one decision and passes). An ask that approves or picks a design, plan, proposal, draft or spec links it in the ask itself, [design](https://…), never a path on a machine or a summary alone; a short link text keeps room under the limit (a subscription or payment plan, software package or compound such as "the design system rollout" needs none). A link in the ask goes to a short decision page made for it (an artifact, a document or a mockup page), never a long project or notes page. With no options listed the Recommend is a yes or a no. The ask line never says I, you or me. "none" or clear_ask=true withdraws it.

ask_by.description: Retired: a call that passes it is refused. The day a wait on another item, a relay or an event comes back to someone if it has not ended is until, YYYY-MM-DD, tomorrow at the earliest: until="<day, within 7 days>".

check.description: What closes the item once work handed to another session is done; the server runs it every minute: check="pr_merged acme/widgets#12" (also item_closed <item id>, lane <session> <lane>, unit_active <unit>.service). A next line that hands the item to a session other than its mover and you needs a check or, instead, an until date as the hand-off's backstop: with a hand-off the date is no wait (unless the item is parked or carries wait_kind, wait_basis or an after link, in this call or stored by an earlier one: then the date stays a wait), the item stays active in the new mover's lane and the hand-off is recorded; a front agent needs neither. check="none" clears it.

clear_rank.description: Retired: refused. Ranks are retired; a call that carries this is refused.

contact.description: The item's contact: the front agent (a user-facing agent) that the owner talks to about it, by its name. Leave it out and the contact is the creator when that is a front agent, else the project's -main agent. A background agent that creates an item may name one of the project's front agents here; any other name is refused, and the refusal lists the project's front agents with their mandates. On an update it changes the contact with the same check; an update that re-files the item under another project (project=) makes that project's -main agent the contact, unless contact is passed too, the contact is a front agent of that project as well, or the contact is the item's creator and a front agent of any project (it stays). The same fall to the -main agent happens when the contact retires.

description.description: The item's background as `- ` bullets, at most 8 lines, every line `- ` included at most 120 characters, live state only (never steps, how-to or commands): description="- Goal: the export finishes in under a minute\n- Problem: the nightly run takes 9 minutes". The first bullet opens `Goal:`, a symptom or cause goes in a later `Problem:` bullet, the owner's words go in a bullet such as `- the owner: …`, and parallel bullets go under one parent bullet, indented two spaces.

done.description: Open steps you finished: positions (1-based, marked steps count) or the exact first line: done=[1] or done=["my-x: build it"]. A step of yours that next leaves out must be here or in dropped.

dropped.description: Open steps that are no longer wanted, named like done: dropped=[2]. A different action is a new line of next, not a reword.

hold.description: Retired beside a date: a call that passes hold with a date is refused. A park is until=<date> with wait_kind="time" and wait_basis (the form is under wait_basis). It reads as waiting, not on agent; clear_hold=true ends a park the item stores. On a relay or event wait no flag is stored (the wait is the park until its day) and the park ends a stored work-in-hand state.

mover.description: Who moves the item now: the owner, a session name or id, or the project's background agent. On an item that waits it is who takes the item when the wait ends. A front agent (a session the owner talks to) only by itself: it gets no hand-off notice, so a create or update from another session that sets mover=<front agent> gets the project's builder instead (the reply and History say so; send it again to keep it; an update by the item's mover (no front agent) or the project's builder that names a live front agent of the project holding the item's first open named step, as the item stands before the write and left open by it, hands it back: kept as sent at once, and a mover is told as a turn; with no builder it is refused, except from a listed session to a front agent of the item's own project: mover= tells it, the others leave it to the answer or the date). A front agent of the item's project may hand it to a sibling front agent on the owner's words: said=[Acked-by …] keeps the sibling in mover, then, post_wake_mover or agent as sent, and mover and agent tell it. On an update that sets no needs, the session needs names for the mover it replaces is swapped for the new one.

next.description: Your lines of the checklist, one step per line, each opening with who takes it, then a space (a label such as `Status:` names no one). It replaces only your own lines: write again every open step of yours that stays and mark the others in done or dropped (or reword) in the same call. Steps 1 and 2 open, step 1 finished: done=[1], next="my-x: test it\nmy-x: open the PR". An item that stays open keeps one open step, a parked one the step its date leads to. Never reword an open step to add progress. next="none" removes your open lines; an empty next is next not passed.

options.description: The alternatives of a decision, one per line: options=[{"label": "Approve", "line": "Approve the schema", "recommended": true}, {"label": "Decline", "line": "Wait a week", "recommended": false}] (2-6 entries, exactly one recommended, each line at most 160 characters). A yes/no decision lists Approve and Decline. Name who acts in every option, label and line (the owner, a session's name, a role), never I, you, we, us or me. A label never opens with a lone letter ("B: strip", "Option C"): the board letters options itself, except with a mockup linked, where it draws them by name in the order given: name them as the mockup does, in its order.
